newsitem.title: GERMANY: German beef consumption down 10 percent - ministry.
newsitem.headline: German beef consumption down 10 percent - ministry.

text.p: The consumption of beef in Germany declined by nearly 10 percent in 1996 while Germans turned away from beef and towards fowl, the agriculture ministry on Friday,
The per-capita beef consumption declined by nearly one kg to 10.5 kg, the ministry said in a statement, while fowl was up 400 grams to 8.4 kg per capita.
The overall meat consumption in Germany was only down by one percent to a per capita average of 62.1 kg.

Germans quickly turned away from beef products in March 1996 after the European Union banned exports of British beef after Britain said mad cow disease, of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), could be transmitted to humans who ate infected meat in the form of Creutzfeld-Jakob Disease (CJD).
The agriculture ministry in Bonn said the percentage of beef consumed by Germans declined to 17.1 percent of the total meat eaten from 20.9 percent in 1995.
